items.answer: The program resends the whole history, including the calendar result, in the input of the next call
accepted: the program includes the earlier results in the next call
the history is sent again each call
the tool result is appended to the messages and sent back to the model
items.rationale: Each step is a separate call; the program appends the tool result to the history and sends the full history again. An answer that the model remembers it shows the belief that the model keeps state between calls.

Each call re-reads the full history: 2,500, then 4,000, then 5,500, then 7,000, and 2,500 + 4,000 + 5,500 + 7,000 = 19,000. Answering 7,000 counts only the last call, and 11,500 adds the start once plus each step once, ignoring the resending.

Chunk and index the manuals and return only the few relevant chunks through a search tool, so each call stays small. Loading everything is costly and degrades recall; summaries lose the exact steps; notes are for small facts, not a 3,000-page library.

items.answer: Wrong: the window only holds the current session and is empty in a new one; save the status outside the window (a record or database) and load it at the start of the next session
accepted: not right; a new session starts with an empty context, so store the training status in a database or notes and load it back
items.rationale: The context window is working memory for one session. Cross-session memory needs saved notes or a record plus a step that loads it into the new context.

items.answer: Embeddings match meaning and can miss exact codes like E-42; add keyword (BM25) search, i.e. hybrid search
accepted: embedding search can miss exact strings; add keyword search
add BM25 keyword matching alongside embeddings
items.rationale: Embedding search matches meaning and may miss an exact identifier; keyword matching (BM25) finds exact strings. Combining both is the fix from the Contextual Retrieval article.
